chunks: Muʿāwiyah said: “And after that I met al-Ṭabarī, Muḥammad, and he informed me, saying: ‘I heard ʿAlī ibn Mūsā (عليه السلام) saying...’”

“The indebted person, when he incurs a debt or borrows concerning a rightful obligation”—the uncertainty is from Muʿāwiyah—“is to be granted a delay of one year. Then if his circumstances become ample, otherwise the Imam (عليه السلام) pays it on his behalf from Bayt al-Māl.”

key_terms.أُجِّلَ سَنَةً: he is granted a delay of one year
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam as the legitimate authority responsible for communal welfare
key_terms.الْمُغْرَمُ: the indebted person burdened by debt
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the public treasury from which communal financial obligations are met
key_terms.فِي حَقٍّ: for a legitimate due or rightful obligation

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kāfī say about giving respite to a debtor and the Imam’s responsibility to pay from Bayt al-Māl?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a debtor who has taken on debt for a legitimate right is to be granted a year of respite. If he remains unable to pay after that, the Imam (عليه السلام) is responsible for settling the debt from Bayt al-Māl, showing the public duty of just leadership toward financially burdened members of the community.
